holidays.name: Just Because Day
holidays.description: This is the day to do something delightfully random and have no explanation ready. Skip down the sidewalk, walk backward, jump in a puddle, compliment a stranger's lawn, or send flowers to a friend. If anyone asks why, you already have your answer.
holidays.origin: This is an unofficial observance. It encourages people to act on a whim and drop the need for a reason.
holidays.funFact: Suggested ways to celebrate include spinning a wheel and then cycling in the opposite direction of the arrow. Whatever you do today, the only explanation you need is 'just because.'

holidays.name: Tarzan Day
holidays.description: This day honors the loincloth-wearing, vine-swinging Lord of the Jungle. Fans mark it with a Tarzan movie marathon, a practice of the famous yell, or a re-read of the original adventures.
holidays.origin: The day marks the anniversary of Tarzan's debut. Edgar Rice Burroughs's story 'Tarzan of the Apes' appeared in All-Story magazine in October 1912, and the character went on to become one of pop culture's biggest icons.
holidays.funFact: Burroughs had never been to Africa when he wrote Tarzan. He also named his California ranch 'Tarzana,' and that ranch became the Los Angeles neighborhood of Tarzana.

holidays.name: National Pots de Crème Day
holidays.description: This day celebrates pots de crème, a silky French custard dessert that is richer and creamier than pudding. It is usually served in tiny pots, and chocolate and vanilla are the classic flavors.
holidays.origin: The dessert comes from France, where its name means 'pots of cream.' Its day on the calendar is an unofficial food observance.
holidays.funFact: Pots de crème are traditionally baked in small lidded cups called 'pots de crème.' Those cups were made for this one dessert.
